label: D2 rare a1->S2 detector, larger after unrewarded a1 S1 and early in episode
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * last_is("a1 S1 u") ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 2) * choice
explanation: Fires almost only at D2 when a1 led rarely to S2 (choice and state are observed at D2); zero at D1/GO and on every other choice/state combination. Within those events its size is largest when the previous trial was a1 S1 unrewarded (+0.57), smaller when the previous trial was rewarded (-0.55) or was also an a1 choice (-0.25), and it shrinks over the episode (-0.05 per decile). A graded policy-logit term (model output) at D2 adds a little (negative weight, more active when the policy is less a1-leaning): the observed-only version without it scores dev 0.60 vs 0.65 with it. Test R^2 beyond timing about 0.67, well above the additive all ceiling of 0.30 because the terms are interactions on the rare a1->S2 event. Hidden good state, since_rev, future reward and the trial two back add nothing.

issues: The score reproduces: dev 0.647 and test 0.667 beyond timing. Timing alone gives 0.03 and the additive 'all' ceiling is 0.30. The D2 rare a1->S2 gating is real: the profile residual for choice x state code 5 is +0.22, every other code is about -0.03, and D1/GO are exactly 0.

The claim that it is 'smaller when the previous trial was rewarded (-0.55)' is wrong as a general statement. I gave each previous-trial pattern its own term inside the a1->S2 event, measured against prev = a1 S1 u, and scored on test. a1 S1 r: -0.52. a1 S2 r: -0.53. a1 S2 u: -0.36. a2 S2 r: +0.56. a2 S2 u: +0.66. a2 S1 r: +0.25. After a2 trials, reward barely matters (a2 S2 r is about as high as a2 S2 u). The prev_reward term is mainly encoding a1 S1 r vs a1 S1 u.

With their terms the claimed set mispredicts specific history classes. After a1 S2 u it predicts about 1.47 - 0.57 = 0.90, but the actual level is close to a1 S1 r (low). After a2 S2 r and a2 S1 r it predicts about 0.6, but the actual level is about 1.1. The R^2 cost is small only because these events are rare.

The real structure is simpler and different. The activation is high when the previous trial was any a2 trial (this a1 choice is a switch; weight +1.16) or a1 S1 unrewarded (+1.11). It is low after a1 S1 rewarded and after either a1 S2 outcome. 'Larger after a1 S1 u, smaller after reward or a1' is a compensating encoding of that pattern.

The policy-logit claim does not hold up. Once previous action is coded properly, the E*choice weight drops to about 0.001 (test 0.649 with it, vs 0.593 without ep_dec/choice). The choice term was proxying for previous-trial history, not adding graded policy information.
The episode decline is confirmed: about -0.05 per decile in every variant. A trial-two-back term adds nothing (0.668), and value adds about 0 (0.669).

Misses: the worst-fit windows are peaks of about 2.0-2.6 predicted at 0.3-1.0, in every term set. Peak magnitude is under-predicted but follows no history class, so it looks like scatter. The tool's 'mean error by phase' is the same for both term sets: D1/GO +0.009, D2 -0.019.
